title: Supplier Trust Accelerator — insurance credit pathways & fastlane procurement
creator: Aisha Romero
description:
Problem: Enterprise procurement cycles are a major friction point for self-serve expansion. Large buyers ask for SOC2 evidence, custom contract clauses, and insurance commitments which delay deals and add manual work to both sales and legal.

Goal: Design and piloting a 'Supplier Trust Accelerator' flow that (1) auto-assesses vendor risk and maps customers to a compact SOC2-lite evidence bundle, (2) offers an automated insurance crediting option (discounted onboarding or escrowed credit tied to insurance proof) to unlock faster approvals, and (3) integrates with a lightweight vendor portal so procurement teams can retrieve artifacts without a SOC2 audit for low/medium risk deals.

Deliverables:
- Requirements doc for SOC2-lite evidence bundle and rubric for risk tiers.
- UX wireframes and portal flow for artifact sharing and insurance upload.
- Pricing experiment matrix tying insurance credit levels to onboarding discounts and SLA credits.
- Pilot contract addendum templates (legal-reviewed) and checklist for Sales to use.
- Success metrics dashboard and A/B experiment plan.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pilot reduces average procurement time for qualified mid-market deals by >=30%.
- At least 25% of pilots opt into insurance credit pathway during sales cycle.
- No unresolved legal blockers for the templated addendum after internal legal review.

Risks & constraints:
- Insurance verification is noisy; we will start with manual verification for pilot and automate later.
- Some enterprise buyers will still require full SOC2; this is targeted at low/medium risk and speed-focused customers only.
- Changes to pricing must be reversible and instrumented for rollback if quality/regression flags surface.

Notes: This is a cross-functional initiative (Sales, Legal, Security, Console, Growth). The first pilot will run with two strategic mid-market customers and a subset of inbound self-serve leads.

Security flagged that encryption KMS integrations require explicit evidence; decided to include KMS key rotation log excerpt in SOC2-lite bundle for mid/low risk. Assigned to Security (Priya) to prepare template snippets.

2026-02-09 — Design: First-pass portal wireframes uploaded to Figma (link: https://re.figma/supplier-trust-accelerator). UX suggests a two-step upload + verification UI with progress state; Console team to assess feasibility for tokenized artifact links.

2026-02-16 — Legal review: Initial addendum OK in principle, but requested explicit limit language for insurance-credit redemption window. Legal (Raj) proposed 90-day redemption window. Updated template in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/supplier-trust/pm-30877-template

2026-02-22 — Engineering scoping: Console infra estimates 3 sprints to ship portal MVP (upload, tokenized link, audit logs). Dependency: backend S3 signed-url policy and access-control flag. ENG ticket created: ENG-11258 (console-portal-mvp).

2026-03-02 — Pricing experiment: Growth proposed matrix with three credit tiers (5%, 10%, 20%) tied to verified insurance amount and annual commit. Decided to run randomized CC experiment on qualifying self-serve signups. Growth owner: Maya. Experiment plan doc: https://drive.redwood/pricing/STA-experiment-v1

2026-03-09 — Pilot customers identified: AcmeRobotics and FinPort (both mid-market). Sales committed to shepherd procurements and capture timelines. Action: Sales to use checklists and record time-to-sign in pilot sheet.
2026-03-12 — Security sign-off required: Added security_review_required flag. Security needs to confirm SOC2-lite artifacts do not expose sensitive internals; scheduled review 2026-03-18.

2026-03-14 — Current: Design and Legal templates are in review. Engineering started gated work on artifact upload endpoint (PR: https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/4501). Next: finalize metrics tracking (time to contract, opt-in rate) and instrument pilot toggle in Console.
